title: Jellystat
name: jellystat
description: Statistics for Jellyfin (and Emby): who watched what, when and on which device, with live sessions, per-library and per-user stats, play history and charts of when people actually watch. Source: https://github.com/CyferShepard/Jellystat

env.name: JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET
env.label: JWT secret (required)
env.description: Signs everyone's logins. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy.

env.name: JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: For the bundled Postgres. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16. Never change it after the first deploy.

env.name: JELLYSTAT_TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Like Europe/London, for which day and hour a play counts towards. Set it before the first deploy, since the database keeps the first one.

env.name: JELLYSTAT_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Fill in the JWT secret and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them (openssl rand -hex 32 and openssl rand -hex 16), and keep both the same on every redeploy. Open it on port 3060: the first visitor makes the Jellystat login, then it asks for your Jellyfin address and an API key (Jellyfin's Dashboard --> API Keys). Do both steps in one go, as anyone can redo the first one until Jellyfin's connected. The address has to be one this container can reach, like http://192.168.1.20:8096, not localhost. It only counts plays from when it's running, but Settings --> Tasks --> Import Playback Reporting Plugin Data brings in older ones if you use that plugin. A few things answer without a login (who's watching right now, your Jellyfin admin users, recently added), so keep it on your own network. Stats live in Postgres (the postgres-data volume), and backups from Settings --> Backup go in jellystat-backups. It checks GitHub for updates and loads a font from Google. Docs: github.com/CyferShepard/Jellystat
